prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a hit while turning left in Houston, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1401; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you were involved in while turning left in Houston. Is it all right if we proceed?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Please describe what happened, in your own words.

A: I was driving through an intersection and wanted to turn left onto the cross street. There was a gap in oncoming traffic, so I started the turn. A vehicle coming the other way hit the front passenger side of my car.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before you began your turn?

A: I saw it, but it looked like it was still a good distance away. I judged that I had time to make the turn.

Q: Was the signal in your favor when you entered the intersection?

A: I believe it had just turned yellow. I was going to make the turn on the arrow, but the arrow had already ended by then.

Q: Did you have any injuries at the scene?

A: I had some neck stiffness right away, but I didn't think much of it. By the next morning the pain had gotten worse, and I had trouble turning my head to the side.

Q: Have you seen a doctor since the collision?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic two days later. They diagnosed whiplash and gave me a neck brace and some medication. I've been going to physical therapy twice a week since then.

Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?

A: Yes. Sitting for long periods makes it worse, and I get headaches at the back of my head most afternoons.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?

A: No, I think that covers it. I'll send over the medical bills and the repair estimate when I have them.

Q: Thank you. That concludes this statement.
